comparison: Perfect agreement on C1 and C2. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the finding that CCL5 expression negatively correlates with clinical outcomes in PDAC patients, validated across multiple cohorts.

Disagreement on C12, C13, C24. OpenEval finds claims supported by experimental data showing limited CCR5i monotherapy efficacy. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, questioning the necessity of CCR5i given its pathogenic effect on tumor growth and lack of impact on NK/CD8+ cells.

Strong agreement on C14, C25-C29. Both evaluations support the triple combination therapy effects (radiation + CCR5i + anti-PD1) showing Treg reduction and enhancement of NK and CD8+ T cells, despite concerns about CCR5i alone.

Agreement on C33-C35. Both support the identification and characterization of CD103+CD49a+ hypoactive NK cells with nearly 40-fold increase after treatment. Peer reviewers affirm the NKG2D-negative, tissue-residency marker expressing NK cell subset.

Agreement on C36-C40, C96. Both support the scRNA-seq identification of NK subpopulations in human PDAC and their correlation with mouse findings. Minor concern from peer reviewer about KLRC2 transcript interpretation not challenging core finding.

Agreement on C42-C44, C83-C84. Both support the CellChat ligand-receptor interaction analysis identifying 32 significant interactions and characterization of signaling pathways between trNK and cDC1 cells.
Agreement on C45-C46. Both support the correlation analysis showing cDC1-dependent relationship between trNK and CD8+ T cells in mouse models and human TCGA data, affirming the trNK-cDC1-CD8 axis.

Agreement on C47-C49. Both support the survival analysis showing trNK signature correlates with outcomes in PDAC and pan-cancer contexts. Peer reviewers emphasize broader interest and high relevance across cancer types.
Agreement on C50, C73-C74. Both support the finding that CCL5high/trNKhigh patients have better outcomes than CCL5high/trNKlow patients, with CCR1-mediated mechanism accepted.

Agreement on C22, C86-C87. Both support the KPC-F murine model characterization and validation, with Treg reduction documented. Peer reviewers implicitly accept model appropriateness without specific concerns.
Agreement on C30. Both support the correlation analysis showing hypoactive NK cells correlate better with tumor control than active NK cells, with statistical support accepted.

Agreement on C88, C90-C91. Both support the multiplex immunofluorescence data showing heterogeneous but overall significant treatment responses, with acknowledgment of responder/non-responder variability.
Agreement on C95, C97. Both support the scRNA-seq clustering and NK subpopulation identification. Peer reviewers praise the elegant use of single-cell sequencing analysis.

Difference in evaluation type on C71-C72. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative interpretations requiring validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the mechanistic interpretation and therapeutic potential as reasonable conclusions with acknowledged limitations.

Agreement on C3-C7. Both support these as established background knowledge from prior work on CCL5-CCR5 signaling. OpenEval notes these represent established knowledge rather than new findings; peer reviewers accept without challenge.
Agreement on C8-C11. Both support these as accurate summaries of prior work (Caushi et al., 2021; Kirchhammer et al., 2022) providing important context. No challenges to the background literature.
Agreement on C19-C21, C55-C58. Both support these clinical context and prior work claims as accurate background with appropriate citations, not representing new findings.

Agreement on C59-C67. Both support these NK cell biology background claims as established knowledge with appropriate citations. Minor clarification from peer reviewer about KLRC2 does not challenge core background.
Agreement on C75-C77. Both support these claims about NKG2D downregulation as grounded in established literature, consistent with observed phenotype in the study.
Agreement on C80-C82. Both support the validation data showing NCAM2 has no prognostic value, NKG2C expression in NK_C1, and validation in second scRNA-seq dataset.

Partial overlap on C78, C85. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the integrated mechanistic model involves substantial speculation requiring validation. Peer reviewers rate related claims (C42-C44, C83-C84) as SUPPORTED, accepting the CellChat analysis without challenging the mechanistic interpretation.

Partial overlap on C70. OpenEval rates C68-C70 as UNCERTAIN within broader mechanistic speculation. Peer reviewers rate C70 as SUPPORTED, acknowledging speculative nature but accepting as reasonable discussion point with noted limitations.
Agreement on C18, C52-C53. Both support the pan-cancer survival analysis showing improved survival across multiple cancer types. Peer reviewers emphasize broader interest and potential significance.

Partial overlap on C54. OpenEval supports the mechanistic claim as involving inference but well-supported. Peer reviewers accept as reasonable interpretation acknowledging limitations in functional validation.
